title: How Your Body Clock Affects Your Mental Health and Ways to Keep It in Sync - Nautilus
gist: Paywall-truncated explainer by Sarah Chellappa on how circadian rhythms affect mood. Both sleep quality and sleep timing affect emotions, and the suprachiasmatic nucleus acts as the master clock, using light signals to coordinate the clocks in other organs.

insights.claim: Poor sleep affects emotions, and the timing of sleep also plays a role in irritability, anxiety and sadness, not just how long or how well people sleep.
insights.speaker: Sarah Chellappa
insights.so_what: Sleep timing is a separate lever for mental health, relevant to shift-work policy and the market for light and sleep products.
insights.quote: Poor sleep affects our emotions, but its timing also plays a role.

insights.claim: Circadian rhythms are nearly 24-hour cycles that regulate alertness, hormones, body temperature and digestion.
insights.speaker: Sarah Chellappa
insights.so_what: Because circadian rhythms touch many body systems, disrupting them has wide health effects.

insights.claim: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a cluster of nerve cells deep in the brain, is the body's master clock. It uses light signals from the eyes to coordinate clocks in the brain, liver, heart and gut.
insights.speaker: Sarah Chellappa
insights.so_what: Light exposure is the main input to the master clock, so lighting design and screen habits matter for health.
